descriptionChirho: To swallow physically or gulp down, whether of a creature consuming prey (Jonah's fish), the earth opening to engulf people (Korah), or enemies overwhelming victims; the basic Qal active sense corresponding to Arabic بَلَعَ (balaʿa, to swallow), Korean 삼키다 (samkida), and Swahili -meza.

To devour or swallow up intensively in the Piel stem, expressing forceful consumption or engulfing, whether literal or figuratively of enemies consuming a people or wealth being devoured; retains the swallowing imagery but with intensified force, consistently rendered with Arabic ابْتَلَعَ (ibtalaʿa, Form VIII intensive) and Korean 삼키다.

To destroy or annihilate in the Piel stem, a fully metaphorical extension where the swallowing imagery is lost and the sense is pure destruction; confirmed by Arabic يُزِيلُ (yuzīlu, to remove) and لِأُهْلِكَ (li-uhlika, to destroy), Korean 파괴함 (destruction) and 멸하게 (to exterminate), and Swahili -haribu (to destroy) and -angamiza (to annihilate).

To confuse, confound, or lead astray in the Piel stem, a distinct semantic development from swallowing up speech or counsel so that clarity is lost; confirmed by Spanish confundir/confundiré, and Swahili -potosha (to mislead), distinguishing this sense from both physical swallowing and metaphorical destruction.

To be swallowed up, consumed, or overwhelmed in the passive stems (Nifal perfect and Pual imperfect/participle), expressing the state of having been devoured or destroyed; Arabic uses passive forms ابْتُلِعَ (ubtuliʿa) and يُبْلَعَ (yublaʿa), Korean 삼켜지다 (samkyeojida, passive of swallow), Swahili -mezwa (passive).

To be engulfed or swallowed up reflexively in the Hitpael stem, describing a process of being overwhelmed or confused that happens to the subject; Spanish se confundía confirms the reflexive/middle voice nuance distinct from the purely passive Nifal/Pual forms.
